topic.title: Close Friends, Not Really
topic.claim: The 'close friends' story feature has quietly turned into a popularity tier, not an actual list of close friends.
topic.behaviour: People add hundreds of names to their close friends list, way more than anyone's real circle.
topic.mechanism: Access became the currency, so people use the feature to manage who feels chosen.
topic.group: Instagram users with a story habit
topic.why_now: close friends lists have quietly bloated for most people over the last year

score.why: A specific, named Instagram feature turned into a status reframe, same move as her 'Instagram made everyone a brand' belief.

topic.send_to: the friend whose close-friends list has 300 people

paragraphs: There's something weird about close friends lists. Most people have about five real close friends. Their list has three hundred. And nobody asks why.
Swipe to read →
Picture the bad hair day, the rant about your landlord, the 2am thought. Those are the posts you'd want a small list for.
Then the list kept getting bigger. Nobody ever left. People only got added.
You add the college group. Then the office people you like. Then the cousin who'd notice if she wasn't there.
Then someone you met once at a wedding, because removing them later feels rude.
That's how ten becomes three hundred.
I check who's on mine more than I'd like to admit. And I notice who's on theirs.
When I can see a friend's close friends story, I feel a tiny bit chosen.
When I can't, I notice that too.
That's the whole thing. The list stopped being about closeness. It became about access.
Being on it means you're inside something. Regular followers get the public version.
Look at what people post there now. It's rarely the ugly stuff anymore.
It's the concert, the dinner, the vacation photo that felt too much for the main story.
Close friends became a VIP section with a velvet rope.
The list isn't for the people on it. It's for you.
You get to decide, quietly, who feels included this week. Nobody gets told. Nobody can complain.
It works like a wedding guest list. Half the names are there because leaving them out would start a conversation.
Nobody checks whether you're actually close. They just check whether they made the cut.
So the real close friends had to move. They're in a WhatsApp group with four people and a stupid name.
That's where the bad hair day goes now.
The close friends list is for everyone else.

hook_candidates.hook: There's something weird about close friends lists. Most people have about five real close friends. Their list has three hundred. And nobody asks why.
Your close friends list has three hundred people on it. Your real close friends left for a four-person WhatsApp group. Think about what that means.
Your Instagram close friends list has almost nothing to do with your close friends. And I know how that sounds.
Nobody adds three hundred people to close friends to share bad hair days. They're quietly deciding something else.
Imagine your close friends list. Three hundred names. Now count the ones you'd actually text at 2am.
